brave/brave-browser#58958.author: kdenhartog
brave/brave-browser#58958.bodyExcerpt: During Orchard-to-Ironwood turnstile migration, the Ironwood output bundle is padded to two actions instead of remaining a single unpadded action as specified in ZIP 318. This causes migration transactions to overpay network fees by 5,000 to 10,000 zatoshis per transfer. Additionally, this creates non-conforming transaction bundle shapes that reduce anonymity set uniformity during migration. brave/brave-browser#58756.title: fix: validate Zcash memo length in bytes
brave/brave-browser#58756.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58756.bodyExcerpt: With Ironwood explicitly enabled on macOS Nightly 1.97.1, a memo containing 171 copies of 界 displays 171/512 without a length error, even though its UTF-8 encoding is 513 bytes and exceeds the 512-byte memo limit. Use the UTF-8 byte length for both the counter and validation so users can correct oversized messages before review; funded submission was not tested. cc @kdenhartog

brave/brave-browser#58754.title: fix: decode extended Zcash address fields with the correct byte order
brave/brave-browser#58754.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58754.bodyExcerpt: Focused tests against the September 4, 2026 master snapshot show that multi-byte Zcash address fields are decoded to the wrong value, such as 256 becoming 1, and unnecessarily long encodings of small values are accepted. Use the specified byte order and require the shortest valid encoding; the long-value failures were reproduced in isolated source tests, and ordinary supported receiver fields are below the affected multi-byte range. cc @kdenhartog

brave/brave-browser#58753.title: fix: recognize valid uppercase and extended Zcash unified addresses
brave/brave-browser#58753.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58753.bodyExcerpt: On macOS Nightly 1.97.1, a valid unified address is rejected when written entirely in uppercase, and adding an unknown optional receiver alongside valid transparent and shielded receivers also causes rejection. Both forms should preserve recognition of usable known receivers under the address-format rules, with the usual migration restrictions still applied. cc @kdenhartog

brave/brave-browser#58752.title: fix: reject malformed Zcash unified addresses before choosing a receiver
brave/brave-browser#58752.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58752.bodyExcerpt: On macOS Nightly 1.97.1, unified addresses with duplicate or out-of-order receivers reach the migration restriction instead of a malformed-address error, while an address with an invalid shielded receiver is accepted as a transparent recipient. Validate the entire unified address before choosing a receiver; the migration restriction still blocks the duplicate and out-of-order cases, and no transaction was sent. cc @kdenhartog

brave/brave-browser#58280.title: fix: rewind each ZCash shielded pool from a valid checkpoint
brave/brave-browser#58280.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58280.bodyExcerpt: After a chain reorganization, Ironwood notes can be rolled back without rolling back the matching commitment state, leaving shielded synchronization inconsistent. Rewind each shielded pool from one of its own valid checkpoints and treat a no-op truncation as an error. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58284.title: fix: remove ZCash checkpoint mark data during reset and truncation
brave/brave-browser#58284.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58284.bodyExcerpt: Deleting shielded checkpoints can leave their associated mark data behind, which can make a later reset and rescan fail. Delete dependent rows explicitly and migrate existing orphaned data. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58281.title: Add Ironwood recipient capability signaling
brave/brave-browser#58281.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58281.bodyExcerpt: An Orchard-formatted recipient is currently treated as Ironwood-capable whenever Ironwood is enabled, although older wallets may not observe the transfer. Require a distinct capability signal or an explicit user warning before routing funds to Ironwood. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58282.title: fix: require provider capability signaling before Ironwood scanning
brave/brave-browser#58282.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58282.bodyExcerpt: Brave cannot currently distinguish an Ironwood-capable provider reporting an empty state from a provider that does not implement Ironwood. Require an explicit capability signal and validate the supplied state before scanning. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58283.title: fix: use checked positions when scanning ZCash notes
brave/brave-browser#58283.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58283.bodyExcerpt: Provider-supplied tree sizes are combined with action offsets without checked arithmetic. Reject ranges that cannot be represented and add boundary coverage before enabling Ironwood. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58288.title: fix: validate ZCash consensus branch identifiers
brave/brave-browser#58288.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58288.bodyExcerpt: Transaction signing accepts the provider-reported consensus branch identifier without checking it against the selected network and block height. Restrict accepted values to the known upgrade schedule. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58287.title: fix: validate ZCash note versions against their shielded pools
brave/brave-browser#58287.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58287.bodyExcerpt: Stored shielded notes are returned without checking that their version matches the requested pool. Reject mismatches before Ironwood spending is enabled. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58286.title: fix: scope retained ZCash checkpoints by account and pool
brave/brave-browser#58286.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58286.bodyExcerpt: Retained shielded checkpoints are shared across accounts, while Ironwood retention is currently ignored. Scope retention by account and pool before Ironwood spending relies on it. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#58285.title: fix: handle invalid ZCash spendable balance sums without crashing
brave/brave-browser#58285.author: iAnonymous3000
brave/brave-browser#58285.bodyExcerpt: An invalid shielded-note balance sum currently terminates the browser instead of returning a recoverable error. Use the existing safe balance-handling pattern and cover the overflow case. Tracks #56872.

brave/brave-browser#54372.title: [Wallet] Standardize private key export functionality across network accounts
brave/brave-browser#54372.author: cryptojennie

brave/brave-browser#53218.title: ZCashTransaction::operator== compares orchard_part_ with itself instead of other
brave/brave-browser#53218.author: dev-doshi
brave/brave-browser#53218.bodyExcerpt: In ZCashTransaction::operator==, the orchard_part_ field is compared against itself rather than the other transaction's orchard_part_. This means two ZCashTransaction objects with different Orchard parts will incorrectly compare as equal. Severity: Medium — affects wallet transaction deduplication and comparison logic for shielded Zcash transactions. PR: https://github.com/brave/brave-core/pull/34256

brave/gate3#335.title: fix(swap): disable Zcash swap/bridge routing
brave/gate3#335.author: onyb
brave/gate3#335.bodyExcerpt: Brave Wallet currently sends a shielded-only unified address (u1...) as the swap recipient for ZEC destinations. Near Intents pays out to whatever recipient it is given, so funds land in a Ironwood shielded pool. Until Ironwood support lands in Brave Wallet, the funds are invisible to the user even if the swap succeeds. We have at least 3 reported incidents (~$4k combined) all confirmed on-chain as Ironwood shielded payouts.

brave/brave-browser#43250.bodyExcerpt: We currently have overly broad rules that don't prevent things like using brave/renderer code in brave/browser and other similar issues. It's also problematic because our chromium process directories are actually at the top level instead of inside another directory like chrome.

stages.label: In release notes
stages.help: A platform changelog (Stable release notes) lists the issue. See which platforms and versions in the details.

stages.label: In a Release build
stages.help: A merged PR is an ancestor of the brave-core tag of a current Release build, but no release note lists it.

stages.label: In a Beta build
stages.help: A merged PR is in a current Beta build. Beta is a pre-release channel.

stages.label: In a Nightly build
stages.help: A merged PR is in a current Nightly build. Nightly is a development channel.

stages.label: Merged, not confirmed in a current build
stages.help: A linked PR is merged, but no current build is confirmed to include it. A group reads “Merged, build presence unknown” when its presence could not be determined in any current build, “Merged, not confirmed in a current build” when some builds were confirmed not to include it and the rest could not be checked, and “Merged, not yet in a checked build” only when every checked build was confirmed not to include it.

stages.label: Merged in a Brave service
stages.help: Merged in a Brave server-side repository (swap backend or field-trial config). It takes effect when Brave deploys it, which is not public, and applies regardless of browser version.

stages.label: PR in progress
stages.help: An open (or draft) pull request exists.

stages.label: Open
stages.help: Open issue with no merged or open PR found.

stages.label: Closed, no linked fix found
stages.help: Closed, but no merged PR or release note is linked (closed as completed, without a reason, or as a duplicate whose records contradict each other). Treat as unknown, not shipped.

stages.label: PR closed without merging
stages.help: The pull request was closed without being merged.

stages.label: Closed as not planned
stages.help: Closed as not planned (won’t fix, invalid, or handled elsewhere). Nothing shipped through this issue; labels such as release-notes/include do not change that.

stages.label: Duplicate
stages.help: Closed as a duplicate. Follow the canonical issue instead.

cellLegend.label: Available
cellLegend.help: Listed in this platform’s Stable release notes at or below the current Stable version, with no contrary flag evidence at the current build and every required source check completed there.

cellLegend.label: In build
cellLegend.help: The code and an enabled-by-default flag are in this build (Beta/Nightly, or Stable without a release note). Not a release announcement.

cellLegend.label: Opt-in (brave://flags)
cellLegend.help: Present but disabled by default; can be turned on in brave://flags.

cellLegend.label: Off by default
cellLegend.help: The feature flag is disabled by default in this build.

cellLegend.label: Off server-side
cellLegend.help: The app code may be present, but Brave’s public server-side code (e.g. its swap backend repository, brave/gate3) switches this off for Zcash, for every client. The deployed service is not public and could differ.

cellLegend.label: Not present
cellLegend.help: The flag or code this capability depends on is not present in this build.

cellLegend.label: Not planned
cellLegend.help: Brave closed the request as not planned.

cellLegend.label: Not verified
cellLegend.help: Not enough evidence that it works on this build: no platform-specific evidence was found, a required source check could not be completed, or a server-side switch it depends on could not be read. This does not mean it is unavailable.

docs.title: Zcash and Address Types
zcashStatements: Zcash is a secure digital currency that helps protect your privacy.
With Zcash, there are two types of addresses:
Transparent addresses: Transactions with transparent addresses, or t-addresses, can be tracked on the Zcash blockchain the same way Bitcoin can.

docs.title: What is Brave Wallet?
zcashStatements: Support transparent and private shielded Zcash transactions.

docs.title: Brave Wallet FAQ
zcashStatements: Brave Wallet supports Ethereum, EVM-compatible chains and L2s, Solana, Bitcoin, Zcash, and Filecoin.

docs.title: How does Brave Wallet differ from other wallets?
zcashStatements: Brave Wallet users can buy, receive, and send crypto assets across multiple chains, including Ethereum, EVM compatible chains, and Solana, Zcash, and Bitcoin.

docs.title: Brave Wallet - Secure Crypto Wallet | Brave
zcashStatements: Private transactions with Zcash
Brave Wallet supports transparent and private shielded Zcash transactions, providing accountability without sacrificing user privacy.

docs.title: Brave Wallet adds shielded Zcash transactions on desktop, with Android and iOS coming soon | Brave
zcashStatements: Brave Wallet adds shielded Zcash transactions on desktop, with Android and iOS coming soon
April 2, 2025 — Starting today, Brave users can conduct shielded Zcash transactions in the browser-native Brave Wallet with the updated desktop release (v1.77).

This integration is part of the ongoing partnership with Zcash/ECC and Filecoin Foundation announced at Mainnet 2023 , which now allows the privacy-preserving Zcash native currency (ZEC) to be bought, sent, and received directly within Brave Wallet.
Adding shielded transactions with Zcash to Brave Wallet gives users a way to send and store crypto privately.
Extending Brave Wallet privacy with Zcash
Zcash aims to solve this problem.
Zcash is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that forked and adapted an early version of the Bitcoin codebase.
Transactions in Zcash can be controlled by either a transparent address (t-addr) or a shielded address (z-addr), allowing users to choose between public and private transactions.

docs.title: Brave Wallet now supports NEAR Intents | Brave
zcashStatements: The Brave Wallet enables multi-chain access right from the Brave browser, and NEAR Intents is the first swap provider that ties together nearly all of our supported blockchains: Bitcoin, Solana, Zcash, Cardano, and EVM (including Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, etc).
Brave Wallet users now have a decentralized way to swap assets like BTC and ZEC that traditionally lack DEX options.
Transparent ZEC to any chain
Any chain to transparent ZEC
Shielded ZEC to any chain
Any chain to shielded ZEC
Additionally, if the user is spending shielded ZEC, they are always returned back to the shielded pool in case of a refund.
Shielded transactions with Zcash in Brave Wallet give users a way to send and store crypto privately.

docs.title: Brave, Electric Coin Co., and Filecoin Foundation announce partnership to bring new privacy tools to Web3 | Brave
zcashStatements: With support from ECC, Brave will integrate the Zcash protocol in the browser’s built-in crypto wallet so users can securely store, send, and receive ZEC alongside other cryptocurrencies.
“I’m excited about integrating Zcash into the Brave web browser because privacy should be normal.
Not only do we hope to make it simple to use ZEC for private transactions, but we also aim to maximize privacy during key moments of purchase or exchange.”

Brave, ECC, and Filecoin Foundation also teased plans on stage to develop a new, privacy-based feature in the Brave browser that will offer private messages and media transmission via the Zcash protocol.
Electric Coin Co. launched Zcash in 2016 and continues to support the protocol and user experience, alongside other developers and teams.
Zcash is a cryptocurrency built to empower economic freedom.
Our vision for Zcash is that it will provide equal access to economic systems and give everyone the ability to participate in economic activity.

limitations: Brave browser GitHub releases: only the 400 most recent GitHub releases are read each run
Brave Community (Discourse) Zcash reports: Discourse search is relevance-ranked and capped at 10 pages × 50 results per term; topics outside wallet categories are kept only with wallet context
Brave server-side signals (gate3 swap routing, brave-variations studies): Repository state is shown; the deployed service could differ and its deployment time is not public
Brave server-side signals (gate3 swap routing, brave-variations studies): 1 earlier study was dropped because no cohort sets a Zcash/Ironwood feature or parameter: iOSWalletWebUIStudy
Official docs (Brave Help Center, brave.com): Help Center HTML is behind a Cloudflare challenge for automated clients; the public Zendesk JSON API is used instead
gaps: Only public sources are read. Private roadmaps, internal Brave repositories, security reviews and chat channels are not visible, so planned work that has no public issue cannot appear here.

GitHub keyword search is capped at 1,000 results per query and ranks by relevance; queries are split by date when needed, but an item that never uses Zcash vocabulary, carries no Zcash label, does not touch Zcash code paths, and is not linked from tracked work can be missed.
Platform changelogs cover Stable releases only. Beta and Nightly evidence is build-level (code ancestry and compiled-in flag defaults), not release announcements.
Flag values are compile-time defaults. Brave can change behaviour at runtime with server-side variations (Griffin) or brave://flags; that runtime state is not public.
The iOS App Store publishes only a marketing version (e.g. 1.96), not the build number, so iOS Release cannot be pinned to a brave-core tag for flag or code checks.
Code ancestry shows a merged commit is part of a build; it does not detect later reverts, and it does not prove a platform exposes the feature in its UI.
The software and version behind Brave’s mainnet Zcash proxy (zcash.wallet.brave.com) are not public, so server-side advisories (e.g. lightwalletd) cannot be mapped to Brave users.
Buy (Meld) provider support for ZEC is decided at runtime by Meld and is not publicly verifiable.

Brave Community search is relevance-ranked and capped; reports there are user statements, not confirmed defects. Help Center HTML is behind a Cloudflare challenge, so only the public Zendesk API (English locale) is read.
X/Twitter, Discord, Telegram, Reddit and the Zcash Community Forum are not monitored.
